chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Ali from Abu Jamilah said, and he narrated to me: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from his father from Abu Jamilah from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: I asked him about the al-Anfal (spoils of war), so he said: 'That which is of the lands whose people perished, and other than that, the al-Anfal is for us.'
And he said: 'The Surah of al-Anfal contains the cutting off of the nose.'
'What Allah conferred upon His Messenger from them, so it is not what you made to gallop against with your horses and camels, but rather Allah gives authority to His messengers over whom He wills.'
And he said: 'Al-Fay' is that which is from properties in which there was no shedding of blood or killing, and the al-Anfal is like that, it is in its position.'

key_terms.الْأَنْفَال: Al-Anfal (spoils of war/gains), specifically referring to lands whose people perished
key_terms.جَدْعُ الْأَنْفِ: Cutting off of the nose (a specific ruling mentioned in this Surah)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between al-Anfal and al-Fay' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between al-Anfal, which specifically denotes lands whose inhabitants perished without major combat, and al-Fay', referring to wealth acquired without bloodshed. He links this to the Quranic verse emphasizing that divine conquest relies on God's will rather than solely on human military exertion, a concept further illuminated by the mention of 'cutting the nose' as a specific punitive measure associated with this category of spoils.
